title: Integral models of rational Frobenius operators
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $E$, $\mathcal O_E$,
a uniformizer $\varpi=\varpi_E$ and $A_n=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$.
Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$,
$g_\gamma$ the geometric-Frobenius automorphism and $\Phi$ the $q$-power
scheme Frobenius of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and $\kappa^{(m)}$ the
comparison isomorphisms of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison].

Let $K_{\mathcal O}\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an integral object
([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]) whose reductions
$K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$,
and let $K_E$ be the same object of the rationalized category
$D^b_c(X,E)=D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi]$ of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] (so $K_{\mathcal O}$ is a lattice of
$K_E$). Let

$$
\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^*K_E\longrightarrow K_E
$$

be an arbitrary morphism of $D^b_c(X,E)$ (for instance the Weil
structure of an $E$-Weil complex, [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]); no
invertibility, and no invertibility on any lattice, is assumed.

*$E$-stage operators.* All functors below at the stage $E$ are the
rationalizations, by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], of the
integral ones: the pullbacks $Lg_\gamma^{i*}$ with their composition
isomorphisms, $R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], the compact-support
base-change isomorphisms $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ along the automorphisms
$g_\gamma^m$, and the stalk functors with the stalk transports
$\tau_{y,m}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]. Put
$\varphi_E^{[m]}=\varphi_E\circ Lg_\gamma^*\varphi_E\circ\cdots\circ
L(g_\gamma^{m-1})^*\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K_E\to K_E$, as in
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map], and define, by the formulas of
[def-trf-frobenius-operators] in the form of
[lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description],

$$
F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi_E^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*},
\qquad
F_{y,m}=\varphi^{[m]}_{E,\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}
$$

on $R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)$ and on $K_{E,\bar y}$, for $m\geq1$ and
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar y$. For $m=1$ and
invertible $\varphi_E$ the first is the compactly supported operator of
[def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius].

*Stalk normalization.* For $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ one has
$\Phi^m\circ\bar y=\bar y$ ([thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points]), whence a
natural identification $\iota_M:M_{\bar y}\cong(L\Phi^{m*}M)_{\bar y}$
for every $M$; as throughout, the stalk transport of
[def-trf-frobenius-operators] is taken in the form
$\tau_{y,m}=(\kappa^{(m)}_M)_{\bar y}\circ\iota_M$, natural in $M$ and
defined with no Weil structure on $M$, at every finite level $A_n$ (this
is the normalization under which the stalk map of the scheme-Frobenius
map $u_m$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map] is $F_{y,m}$). On integral
objects $\tau_{y,m}$ is the derived limit of these levelwise isomorphisms
on the reduction tower, and at the stage $E$ its rationalization. For a
Frobenius coefficient morphism $\psi$ on $K_n$ with iterates $\psi_m$,
the stalk endomorphism of $K_{n,\bar y}$ is
$\psi_{m,\bar y}=(\psi_m)_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}$, as in the
coefficient-morphism trace formula of the trace-formula chapter.

Then:

1. *Clearing denominators.* There are an integer $N\geq0$ and a morphism
$u:Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O}\to K_{\mathcal O}$ of
$D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ with $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$ in
$D^b_c(X,E)$; that is, $\varpi^N\varphi_E$ maps the lattice into itself.
1. *Integral Frobenius coefficient morphisms.* For such $(N,u)$ let
$u_n:Lg_\gamma^*K_n\to K_n$ be the reduction of $u$ modulo $\varpi^n$
and put
$$
\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}:L\Phi^*K_n\longrightarrow K_n .
$$
Each $\psi_n$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism on $K_n$ in the sense
of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (in general not
invertible), the $\psi_n$ are compatible with the transitions
$K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong K_n$, and the iterates are
$$
\psi_{n,m}=u_n^{[m]}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n},\qquad
u_n^{[m]}=u_n\circ Lg_\gamma^*u_n\circ\cdots\circ L(g_\gamma^{m-1})^*u_n .
$$
1. *Global operator.* For every $n,m\geq1$,
$$
F_{c,m}(\psi_n)=T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})
=R\Gamma_c(X,u_n^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}
\quad\text{on }R\Gamma_c(X,K_n).
$$
Let $U_m=R\Gamma_c(X,u^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ be the integral
endomorphism of $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})=R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma_c(X,K_n)$;
it is the derived limit of the levelwise operators $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)$
(the realization of the graph operators $T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})$), and
$$
\boxed{\,F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}\,\bigl(U_m\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr)
\quad\text{on }R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.\,}
$$
1. *Local operators.* For $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ the stalk
endomorphism of $\psi_{n,m}$ is $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}=u^{[m]}_{n,\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}$
on $K_{n,\bar y}$; the integral endomorphism
$U_{y,m}=u^{[m]}_{\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}$ of $K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$
reduces modulo $\varpi^n$ to $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}$, and
$$
\boxed{\,F_{y,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}\,\bigl(U_{y,m}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr)
\quad\text{on }K_{E,\bar y}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.\,}
$$

Replacing $(N,u)$ by $(N+1,\varpi u)$ multiplies $U_m,U_{y,m}$ by
$\varpi^m$ and leaves the right-hand sides unchanged. *Example:* for
$X_0=\Spec\mathbf F_q$, $K_E=E^2$ and $\varphi_E=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$,
one may take $N=0$ and $u=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$ on
$\mathcal O_E^2$; no rescaling $c\,\varphi_E$ ($c\in E^\times$) is invertible
on any lattice, since its eigenvalues $c,c\ell$ are not both units, but
$\psi_n=u\bmod\varpi^n$ is a (non-invertible) Frobenius coefficient
morphism.

proof.text:
*(1).* By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] the morphisms of
$D^b_c(X,E)$ are
$\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)}(Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O},K_{\mathcal O})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$,
the rationalized pullback being that of the integral one
([prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]). Since $E=\mathcal O_E[1/\varpi]$,
every element of $H\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E=H[1/\varpi]$, for an
$\mathcal O_E$-module $H$, has the form $u\otimes\varpi^{-N}$ with
$u\in H$ and $N\geq0$. Explicitly, write a tensor element as a finite sum $\sum_j h_j\otimes(a_j/\varpi^{e_j})$, choose $N=\max_j e_j$ (take $N=0$ for an empty sum), and put $u=\sum_j a_j\varpi^{N-e_j}h_j$. Balancing gives $\sum_j h_j\otimes(a_j/\varpi^{e_j})=u\otimes\varpi^{-N}$. This is $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$.

source.place: clause *(1)*, with the displayed elementary expansions and cited tower constructions

proof.text: *(2a).* The factorization [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] gives $F_X^{(q)}=g_\sigma\circ\Phi$, hence $\Phi=g_\gamma\circ F_X^{(q)}$ with $\gamma=\sigma^{-1}$, in the orientation of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Each $A_n$ is finite and annihilated by a power of $\ell\ne p$, so [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] applies. The tower reduction of $u$ exists by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Apply [lem-trf-frobenius-coefficient-reduction-coherence] to identify its source with $Lg_\gamma^*K_n$ and to commute $\kappa$ with its transitions. Thus $\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}:L\Phi^*K_n\to K_n$ is a compatible family of Frobenius coefficient morphisms, by [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism].

*(2b).* Induct on $m$, starting with $\psi_n=u_n\kappa$. The recursion of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] and the induction hypothesis give
$$\psi_{n,m}=u_n\kappa_{K_n}\,L\Phi^*(u_n^{[m-1]})\,L\Phi^*(\kappa^{(m-1)}_{K_n}).$$
Naturality of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] at $u_n^{[m-1]}$ replaces the middle two factors by $Lg_\gamma^*(u_n^{[m-1]})\kappa_{Lg_\gamma^{(m-1)*}K_n}$. Multiplicativity of that comparison then replaces the last two comparison factors by $\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n}$. The remaining composite is $u_n^{[m]}$ by its displayed definition in the item. Thus $\psi_{n,m}=u_n^{[m]}\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n}$. The same recursion and the pullback-composition compatibility of [lem-trf-frobenius-coefficient-reduction-coherence] show that $u^{[m]}$ reduces to $u_n^{[m]}$.

*(3a).* The first equality $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)=T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})$ is [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism]. Step (2b) writes $\psi_{n,m}=v\kappa^{(m)}$ with $v=u_n^{[m]}$. Since $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$, the arbitrary-map clause of [prop-trf-graph-frobenius-operator] applies without invertibility of $v$ or a Weil structure. It gives
$$F_{c,m}(\psi_n)=R\Gamma_c(X,u_n^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}.$$

*(3b).* For $a_X:X\to s$ use the exact linear tower lift of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], with one compactification over $k_0$ at every level. By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] its realization is integral compact support, including on morphisms. The integral compact-support exchange is the realization of the specified system mate $e_{a_X}^c$ by [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (2). The reduction comparison [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identifies the reduction tower of $N=Ra_{X!}K_{\mathcal O}$ with these levelwise outputs, coherently with the exchange comparisons; integral bounded constructibility is part of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For this $N$, [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-realization] identifies its integral point transport with the realization of the finite transports. By [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] these two factors give the one-step compact-support transport. The $m$-fold transport of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] is a finite composite with the canonical pullback comparisons; their quotient coherence is [lem-trf-frobenius-coefficient-reduction-coherence]. A functor preserves that composite. Step (2b) similarly identifies the reductions of $u^{[m]}$. Applying realization to the composite tower map therefore gives
$$U_m=R\Gamma_c(X,u^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}=R\varprojlim_n F_{c,m}(\psi_n).$$
Here the input is an actual system morphism, rather than separate levelwise classes.

source.place: clause *(3)*, coherent tower and point-transport realization

proof.text:
*(3c).* By [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] the rationalized pullbacks and $R\Gamma_c$ act on morphisms by $f\otimes\lambda\mapsto F(f)\otimes\lambda$ and preserve the integral comparison maps. Composition in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is $E$-bilinear. Each of the $m$ factors in $\varphi_E^{[m]}$ therefore contributes $\varpi^{-N}$, giving
$$\varphi_E^{[m]}=\varpi^{-Nm}u^{[m]}.$$
Apply the rationalized compact-support functor and compose with the rationalization of $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$. By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] its object is $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\otimes E$. Bilinearity gives
$$F_{c,K_E}^{m}=\varpi^{-Nm}(U_m\otimes E).$$

*(4a).* The prescribed normalization and step (2b) give
$$\psi_{n,m,\bar y}=(u_n^{[m]})_{\bar y}(\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n})_{\bar y}\iota_{K_n}=(u_n^{[m]})_{\bar y}\tau_{y,m}.$$
Apply [lem-trf-completed-stalk-frobenius-reduction], which identifies the reductions of both the completed stalk and its normalized transport. Its naturality carries the reduction of $u^{[m]}_{\bar y}$ to $(u_n^{[m]})_{\bar y}$. Since reduction preserves composition, $U_{y,m}=u^{[m]}_{\bar y}\tau_{y,m}$ reduces to $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}$.
At the $E$ stage [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] extends the point fiber by $-\otimes E$, and [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] extends completed pullback linearly. Step (3c) thus gives $\varphi^{[m]}_{E,\bar y}=\varpi^{-Nm}(u^{[m]}_{\bar y}\otimes E)$. The rational transport is the scalar extension of the integral one by the statement's normalization. Composing yields $F_{y,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}(U_{y,m}\otimes E)$.

source.place: clause *(4)*, completed stalk reductions and rational scalar calculation

proof.text: *(4b).* Replacing $u$ by $\varpi u$ multiplies each of the $m$ factors in its iterate by $\varpi$, hence multiplies $U_m,U_{y,m}$ by $\varpi^m$ and cancels the extra factor from $N+1$. This uses the linear transport of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. For the example take $\mathcal O_E^2$ with coefficient map $u=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$ on the constant object at $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Suppose $T=c\varphi_E$ acts bijectively on a lattice $L$. Choose $b\ge0$ with $\varpi^b\mathcal O_E^2\subset L\subset\varpi^{-b}\mathcal O_E^2$: bound the finitely many coordinates of lattice generators for the upper inclusion, and express the standard basis in a basis drawn from $L$ and clear its denominators for the lower inclusion. For every $j\in\mathbf Z$, $T^j(\varpi^be_1)=\varpi^bc^je_1$ and $T^j(\varpi^be_2)=\varpi^b(c\ell)^je_2$ belong to $L$. Thus $b+jv(c)\ge-b$ and $b+jv(c\ell)\ge-b$ for all positive and negative $j$. These inequalities force $v(c)=v(c\ell)=0$, contradicting $v(\ell)>0$. No unproved lattice or eigenvalue lemma is used here.

split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes clause (1); steps 2–3 clause (2); steps 4–6 clause (3); steps 7–8 clause (4) and its concluding remarks.

tool_uses.why: Generic scalar-localization transport of supplied linear functors and transformations; sk-d-weil does not construct scalar localization.
Natural multiplicative comparison of the two Frobenius pullbacks, used as the fixed comparison interface of the unit.
Generic coherent derived tower lift of compact support, needed to take limits on morphisms; no such tower construction is given by sk-d-weil.

The existing finite-field factorization identifies the model Frobenius with geometric Galois Frobenius composed with absolute Frobenius; Step 2 uses it to fix the comparison orientation after the scheme-Frobenius definition changed.
Generic integral compact-support quotient comparison identifies the reduction tower of Ra_!K with Ra_{!,n}K_n, with the exchange comparisons; the unit does not prove this coefficient theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NY-98f185409 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of the mathematics. The item statement is byte-identical to the main-20261015 blueprint, so nothing is weakened. I checked the coefficient categories: the completed O_E-sheaf category, finite A_n coefficients, and the raw localization at E with no Karoubi completion. The base change g^{m,*}_{gamma,c} is built from FrEx_! = beta_! L(e^c_f) alpha_! (square-exchange (2)) and the point transport iota (def-weil-frobenius-point-transport with inverse-image comparison (b)), and step 3b uses exactly that. The orientation Phi = g_gamma Fr^(q) follows from gamma = sigma^{-1} and the factorization. I checked all eight steps against the cited statements. Step 2a satisfies the hypothesis of the scheme-Galois comparison (A_n finite and ell-primary). The induction in step 2b is correct: naturality and multiplicativity of kappa, base case m=1. Step 3a uses the graph-operator clause for an arbitrary, possibly non-invertible v with K_n ctf. Step 3b realizes an actual tower morphism, using the tower functor for a_X and lem-fix-operation-reduction. The scalar varpi^{-Nm} in steps 3c and 4a is correct. The lattice-valuation argument in step 4b is correct for ramified E. The three new unsplit nodes are true, strictly smaller than the item's clauses, and not duplicates. The coherence lemma covers the pullback-reduction comparisons and kappa^(m) across quotients A_b -> A_a, which neither the scheme-Galois comparison nor thm-trf-finite-coefficient-map state. The point-transport lemma says the integral iota_N is the realization of the finite iota_{N_n}, and I checked it against the cone map z -> (0, theta(z)). The completed-stalk lemma follows lem-pur (1) and lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction and reduces tau_{y,m} to tau_{y,m,n}; it is distinct from lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction and from prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems, which would make a cycle. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there are no cycles. The searches are recorded in all required kinds, and no SGA is cited. I accept the five declared tool_uses, including the new lem-fix-operation-reduction. The item's maintainer tool_uses field still lists lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site and lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible, which its proof no longer cites; the merge tool can prune them. Edge cases checked: K=0, u=0, N=0, m=n=1, empty X, and X_0=Spec F_q. No changes.
